description: One of the largest land predators ever, with a massive skull, bone-crushing teeth the size of bananas, and surprisingly tiny two-fingered arms. It ruled the floodplains of western North America at the very end of the age of dinosaurs.
interestingFacts: Its bite was the strongest of any land animal ever measured — over 5 tonnes of force.
Despite its size, some scientists think it could jog at around 20 km/h.
A famous specimen named Sue is the most complete T. rex ever found.

description: A tank-like plant-eater with two long brow horns, a shorter nose horn, and a huge bony neck frill. It lived alongside Tyrannosaurus rex and could defend itself against it.
interestingFacts: Its skull could be over 2.5 metres long — one of the largest of any land animal.
It sheared through tough plants with hundreds of teeth stacked in batteries.
Fossils show healed horn injuries, evidence of real battles.

description: A fast, feathered hunter about the size of a turkey — much smaller than in the movies. It used a large sickle-shaped claw on each foot to pin down its prey in the deserts of Mongolia.
interestingFacts: A famous fossil preserves one locked in combat with a Protoceratops.
Quill knobs on its arm bones prove it had feathers.
Its sickle claw could grow to about 6.5 cm long.

description: Instantly recognisable by the two rows of big bony plates along its back and the four long tail spikes it swung at attackers. Its brain was famously tiny — about the size of a walnut.
interestingFacts: The spiky tail weapon is nicknamed the 'thagomizer'.
Its back plates may have flushed with blood to change colour.
An Allosaurus fossil has a wound matching a Stegosaurus tail spike.

description: A giraffe-like giant whose front legs were longer than its back legs, tilting its long neck up to browse treetops other dinosaurs couldn't reach — up to 9 metres above the ground.
interestingFacts: It's named 'arm lizard' because of those long front legs.
It swallowed leaves whole — no chewing — and let its stomach do the work.
It was the first dinosaur shown in the movie Jurassic Park.

description: One of the longest dinosaurs known from good skeletons, built like a suspension bridge with a whip-like tail longer than its neck. Casts of its skeleton stand in museums all over the world.
interestingFacts: Its tail had about 80 vertebrae and may have cracked like a whip.
It likely stripped leaves from branches with comb-like front teeth.
Steel tycoon Andrew Carnegie funded the famous specimen 'Dippy'.

description: Longer than T. rex, with a crocodile-like snout for catching fish and a spectacular 1.7-metre sail on its back. It's the best candidate we have for a swimming dinosaur.
interestingFacts: The original fossils were destroyed in a WWII bombing raid on Munich.
New fossils show it had a tall paddle-like tail for swimming.
Its nostrils sat high on its skull, handy for a life around water.

description: A living fortress covered in bony armour plates, with a huge club of solid bone at the end of its tail that could swing hard enough to break a predator's leg.
interestingFacts: Even its eyelids had bony armour.
The tail club could weigh more than 20 kilograms.
It kept its soft belly close to the ground — flipping it over was the only way in.

description: The top predator of the Late Jurassic, with short horns above its eyes and a mouth that opened extremely wide. It hunted the great plant-eaters of its time, possibly in groups.
interestingFacts: More than 46 individuals were found in one Utah quarry alone.
It may have used its upper jaw like a hatchet to slash prey.
It lived 80 million years before T. rex — they never met.

description: A duck-billed dinosaur with a long, curved tube of bone sweeping back from its head. The hollow crest worked like a trombone, letting it make deep honking calls across the herd.
interestingFacts: Scientists have recreated its call with computer models — a low foghorn sound.
The crest could be over 1 metre long.
It could walk on two legs or four.

description: A heavyweight cousin of Diplodocus with a thicker, more powerful build. For a century it was better known by its other name — Brontosaurus, the 'thunder lizard'.
interestingFacts: Its neck bones were unusually wide and strong — maybe for neck-wrestling contests.
A single thigh bone can be taller than an adult human.
The Brontosaurus name was recently argued back to life for a close relative.

description: One of the very first dinosaurs ever named, famous for the sharp thumb spikes it used like daggers. Dozens of complete skeletons were found together deep in a Belgian coal mine.
interestingFacts: Early scientists thought its thumb spike was a horn on its nose.
It was only the second creature ever called a 'dinosaur'.
It could grip branches with a bendy little finger.

description: The famous head-butting dinosaur, with a domed skull roof up to 25 centimetres thick surrounded by a crown of bony knobs. Rivals may have rammed each other like bighorn sheep.
interestingFacts: Its skull dome was 20 times thicker than a human skull.
Some skulls show healed injuries from head-on collisions.
Young ones had flat heads that domed as they grew.

description: A South American sprinter with two devil-like horns over its eyes and arms even stubbier than T. rex's. Its huge leg muscles made it one of the fastest big predators ever.
interestingFacts: Skin impressions show it was covered in rows of scaly bumps.
Its arms were so short they had almost no use at all.
It may have sprinted at over 50 km/h.

description: An early predator wearing two thin, rounded crests on its head like a double mohawk. The real animal was much bigger than the movies show — and there's no evidence it spat venom.
interestingFacts: It was the largest land predator of its time in North America.
The movie frill and venom were pure fiction.
Its fossils were found on Navajo Nation land in Arizona.

description: A chicken-sized speedster that chased lizards and insects across Jurassic lagoon islands. For over a century it held the record as the smallest known dinosaur.
interestingFacts: One fossil still has a whole lizard inside its stomach.
It lived on the same islands where Archaeopteryx flew.
Its name means 'elegant jaw' for its delicate skull.

description: The raptor that changed science: its build convinced researchers that dinosaurs were fast, warm-blooded and bird-like. The Jurassic Park 'Velociraptors' were really modelled on it.
interestingFacts: Its study kick-started the 'dinosaur renaissance' of the 1960s.
Several skeletons found together hint that it hunted in packs.
Its killing claw stayed razor-sharp by never touching the ground.

description: Possibly the largest land animal that ever lived — as heavy as ten elephants. It's known from just a few colossal bones, including vertebrae taller than a person.
interestingFacts: A single backbone vertebra measures 1.6 metres tall.
Hatchlings the size of a cat grew 25,000 times heavier as adults.
It was discovered by a rancher who thought a bone was petrified wood.

description: The dinosaur with the longest claws of any animal ever — up to a metre each. Despite the terrifying scythes, this pot-bellied giant used them to hook leafy branches, not prey.
interestingFacts: Scientists first thought its claws belonged to a giant turtle.
Its claws could reach 1 metre — the longest of any known animal.
It was a plant-eater descended from meat-eating ancestors.

description: The punk rocker of horned dinosaurs: four to six long spikes fanned out from its frill, with a half-metre horn on its nose. The display probably impressed rivals and mates alike.
interestingFacts: Its nose horn alone could be 57 centimetres long.
Huge bone beds show its herds numbered in the hundreds.
Each individual's frill spikes were arranged slightly differently.

description: A duck-billed dinosaur with a tall, rounded crest like an ancient Greek helmet. Air looping through the hollow crest gave each animal its own deep, resonant voice.
interestingFacts: One fossil preserved skin impressions over much of the body.
Its crest shape changed with age and differed between sexes.
It had up to 600 tiny teeth for grinding plants.

description: A Jurassic predator with a blade-like horn on its nose, small horns over its eyes, and a row of little armour plates down its back — unique among meat-eaters.
interestingFacts: It's the only known meat-eater with bony armour along its spine.
Its teeth were enormous for its body size.
It competed with the bigger Allosaurus for the same prey.

description: A fish-hunting cousin of Spinosaurus found in an English clay pit, named for the huge 31-centimetre claw on each thumb. Its crocodile-like jaws held nearly a hundred teeth.
interestingFacts: Fish scales and a young Iguanodon were found in its stomach.
It was discovered by an amateur fossil hunter, a plumber named William Walker.
It's one of the most complete big predators ever found in Britain.

description: A sheep-sized early relative of Triceratops with a bony frill but no big horns. Whole herds, nests and even eggs were found preserved in Mongolia's Gobi Desert sands.
interestingFacts: Its skeletons may have inspired the legend of the griffin.
A famous fossil shows one frozen mid-fight with a Velociraptor.
Dozens were found in every size from hatchling to adult.
